A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UltraDelta research. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original compression experiments on language, vision and multimodal models, together with component ablations, sensitivity tests and representation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds evaluations on recent LLMs, storage-format comparisons and controlled fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same variance-based sparsity allocation, quantization and group-wise pruning, trace-norm rescaling and model reconstruction. Appendix A's non-quantized variant is also unchanged. The new storage accounting does not revise these proposed procedures.

E1.justification: v3 adds HumanEval+, MBPP+, MATH, GPQA, MMLU and BBQ evaluations in Table 2, extending coverage to additional coding, mathematical reasoning, knowledge and bias-question-answering benchmarks. The earlier language, vision and multimodal datasets remain.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator families remain unchanged. However, Figure 4(b)'s final-layer similarity-distribution comparison replaces DARE with magnitude pruning while retaining Delta-CoMe, changing comparator participation within that analysis.

E3.justification: v3 includes sparse-index costs in compression-ratio evaluation through Golomb coding and changes baseline matching from equal index-free ratios to similar index-inclusive ratios, with revised sparsities documented in Table 8. Added experiments also introduce recent LLM configurations and controlled fine-tuning from 1,000 to 10,000 steps.

E4.justification: v3 adds comparisons across index-free storage, Golomb coding, CSR and BCSR in Table 7, plus controlled experiments testing how compression benefits depend on model fitting in Appendix D.1/Table 14. Figure 4's representation comparison is revised. Earlier component, DAC, rescaling and hyperparameter analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice; the theoretical variance derivations do not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported compression ratios change substantially: T5-base moves from 800× to 224.6× while its 86.74 score remains unchanged. Compression-matched baseline scores are replaced under revised settings, such as 13B DARE's average changing from 32.20 to 40.23. v3 also adds recent-LLM, storage-format and training-step results and revises Figure 4's similarity findings.

T1.justification: Section 3.3.1 adds an MSE distortion definition and Gaussian rate–distortion reasoning beyond the existing entropy argument. New Appendix B.3 introduces sparsity assumptions and an entropy-based compression-ratio derivation. The original Gaussian entropy and activation-error proofs remain.

C1.justification: The abstract materially narrows the headline compression claims: maxima change from 133×, 800×, 400× and 40× to approximately 50×, 224×, 132× and 18× for LLMs, general NLP, vision and multimodal models respectively. The data-free novelty claim, three-component contribution and broad performance-preservation claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 discusses overfitting and underfitting but emphasizes reducing overfitting; v3 argues that benefits primarily occur in underfitted models, drawing on Table 14. It also adds a deployment-efficiency limitation, explains BCSR's poor suitability and expands the inference-overhead discussion while retaining the heuristic-rescaling limitation.

D1.justification: v3 newly declares code availability, identifies lm-evaluation-harness and EvalPlus, expands the checkpoint-ID table, and documents storage calculations and baseline sparsities in Appendix B.3/Table 8. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the evaluation-framework disclosure alone does not establish that retained experiments changed frameworks.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds ComPEFT and additional layer-wise pruning work and expands its discussion of hybrid compression and DeltaZip's deployment focus. References supporting new benchmarks, models, evaluation frameworks and information-theoretic analysis are added. The central positioning as a data-free hybrid compression approach remains.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and appendix organization remain recognizable. v3 locally rewrites related work, results and discussion, numbers the four effectiveness-analysis subsections, adds acknowledgements and updates affiliations and publication information. The core method exposition is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds dedicated tables for recent LLMs, storage formats, practical versus ideal ratios with sparsities, and training-step experiments. Figures 1, 4 and 6 are revised, including compression labels, plotted comparisons and Figure 1's pruning-marker legend. The pipeline, trace-norm and DAC plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves a central weakness: v2's headline ratios omitted sparse-index costs, whereas v3 distinguishes ideal bounds from index-inclusive estimates and adjusts baseline matching. Added benchmark, storage and controlled-fitting evidence strengthens validation and applicability discussion. Important qualifications remain: Appendix B.3 inconsistently uses symbol counts and bit widths, and its stated T5 setting does not reproduce the reported 224.6× ratio. These defects limit numerical confidence but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in evaluation and transparency.
